title: Statutory adherence to current USP standards by pharmacies licensed under M.G.L. c. 112, ss. 39G, 39H and 39I
subtopic: Statutory USP adherence by compounding pharmacy licensees
rule_summary: M.G.L. c. 112, s. 39G(a)(1) directs the board to establish a category of pharmacy licensure for retail pharmacies engaged in sterile compounding, s. 39H(a)(1) a category for retail pharmacies engaged in complex non-sterile compounding, and s. 39I(a)(1) a category for institutional pharmacies engaged in sterile compounding. Under s. 39G(a)(4) and s. 39I(a)(5) a retail or institutional sterile compounding pharmacy licensed by the commonwealth shall adhere to the most current standards established by USP, all chapters, when engaging in any form of sterile compounding, and under s. 39H(a)(4) a retail complex non-sterile compounding pharmacy licensed by the commonwealth shall do so when engaging in any form of complex non-sterile compounding; each such pharmacy shall also adhere to the additional regulations promulgated by the board pursuant to subsection (c) of its section. Under subsection (c)(4) of each section the board shall promulgate regulations for the administration of paragraphs (1), (2) and (3) of that subsection, provided that no such regulation shall exempt the pharmacy from compliance with the most current standards established by USP, all chapters. As used in s. 39D and in ss. 36E to 42D, inclusive, unless the context clearly requires otherwise, s. 39D(a) defines USP as the current edition of the United States Pharmacopeia and the National Formulary.
exam_relevance: Tests that, for a pharmacy holding a retail sterile, retail complex non-sterile or institutional sterile compounding licence, adherence to the most current USP standards in the licensed compounding is a statutory duty that runs alongside the Board's additional regulations, and that no regulation made for those pharmacies under subsection (c) may exempt them from it.

authority.name: Massachusetts General Laws c. 112
authority.section: M.G.L. c. 112, s. 39D(a), definition of USP

common_confusions: The statutory duty names USP, all chapters, rather than a single chapter.
In these statutes USP is a defined term: the current edition of the United States Pharmacopeia and the National Formulary.
The statutory duty and the Board's additional regulations under subsection (c) apply together; the regulations made for these pharmacies may not exempt them from the most current USP standards.

The duty attaches when the licensed pharmacy engages in the compounding its licence covers: any form of sterile compounding under ss. 39G and 39I, and any form of complex non-sterile compounding under s. 39H.
verification_notes: Read on 2026-09-16 in the text of M.G.L. c. 112, ss. 39D, 39G, 39H and 39I on malegislature.gov, with s. 39F and s. 39J read for context.
